newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Phillips optimistic on SAfrica oil exploration.
newsitem.headline: Phillips optimistic on SAfrica oil exploration.

text.p: Phillips Petroleum Co said on Tuesday it was optimistic about exploration prospects off South Africa's east coast and believed the area held promise.

In May Phillips signed an agreement with the South African government to explore 14.5 million acres off South Africa's east coast -- stretching from the Mozambican border to just above the port city of Durban.

Phillips senior vice president Knut Am told a sub-Saharan Oil and Minerals conference that some industry figures had questioned the decision to explore the east coast while most other exploration took place on South Africa's west coast.
But he said the U.S.-based company believed the area held promise. "There is potential in this area...we are cautiously optimistic," Am said.
Phillips would operate the exploration concession and hold a 40 percent interest with other partners.
Co-venturers in the agreement are Energy Africa Bredasdorp Pty Ltd, an independent South African exploration and production company, PanCanadian Petroleum Ltd and Sasol Ltd with 20 percent each.
Am said the company, ranked among the top 10 U.S. petroleum firms, was active in exploration in 16 other countries.
In addition to South Africa, Phillips was active in Nigeria, Algeria and Tunisia.
Am said with Africa on the road to economic recovery, there would be more markets for oil and gas.
"There is the potential for emerging oil and gas markets," he said.
